trigger: 24h/7d/custom window on a host with more than about 1,100 process rows or 10,000 tcp rows in the window, then pick an older hour
classification_rationale: UI presents the Hour list, tree and per-name connections as the complete answer; the answer is cut silently at the agent (10,000-row default max_rows in execute_user_query, echo_db.hpp:826-827, truncation logged agent-side only, echo_db.cpp:3319; `__total__` counts the cut set) and again by single-frame polling (poll_command keeps one stored response while the agent flushes each 64 KB as its own frame, agent.cpp:286,367)
summary: Silent truncation presented as a complete answer. The /run queries use `ORDER BY hour_ts DESC LIMIT 100000` (process) and `LIMIT 20000` (tcp, dns, arp) over a window of up to 168 hours, but the agent caps at 10,000 rows and poll_command reads one frame (about 64 KB, roughly 1,100 process rows); nothing server-side detects or says so. Oldest hours drop out of the Hour selector, tree and connections; a later frame without `__schema__` parses to 0 rows and shows 'No process activity recorded'; the detail panel says 'No TCP connections recorded under this name in this hour'. render_hour_select also emits no `selected` option, so a requested hour absent from the answer shows the newest hour in the box while banner and tree show the requested one. Fix shape: query only the selected hour (`hour_ts = H`) plus a `SELECT DISTINCT hour_ts ... LIMIT 168` for the selector, merge all frames of a command id, mark a result at or above the agent cap as incomplete, log device/command/rows, and pin the current LIMIT-text assertions that will change.

reviewed_at_sha: d394d35ba (merge-base origin/dev 6288ea8ee; origin/dev at 416cf12d2 is 132 commits ahead, merge-tree clean)
trigger: same (name,user) under more than one parent in an hour, or a parent without a start row in the hour, or parent name differing in case
classification_rationale: build_echo_process_tree evaluates the suspicious-spawn check once per (name,user) node, on the first row's parent after tree linking and cycle cut; the agent keys rows by (name,user,parent_name) so several parents per node per hour is normal; the header contract says 'one deterministic parent' but row order is unpinned (ORDER BY hour_ts only)
summary: Anomaly (suspicious parent->child spawn) undercount and nondeterminism. Harness-verified: cmd.exe under explorer.exe then under winword.exe gives anomalies=0 (reverse order gives 1); a wscript.exe<->cmd.exe cycle gives 0; a parent that ran all hour (no start row that hour) gives 0; WINWORD.EXE vs winword.exe link mismatch gives 0; counts of all parents are summed under the first parent (cmd.exe 1+1 under winword and 2 under explorer reads 'started 4' under winword). The banner 'N flagged' and Anomalies-only therefore silently hide detections. Fix: evaluate echo_is_suspicious_spawn(row.parent_name,row.name) on every stored row, independent of linking and the cycle cut (it already lower-cases basenames), keep a bounded list of distinct parents per node, add name,user,parent_name to the ORDER BY, and say 'also started by' in the detail.

trigger: a Linux/macOS process whose comm contains '|' or a newline
classification_rationale: walk_schema_rows accepts rows with MORE cells than the schema (`cells.size() <= need` only) and drops malformed rows without a count; the agent writes raw column text joined by '|' one row per line (echo_plugin.cpp:4706-4723) and only echo_proc_perf sanitises '|'; the header comment 'a forged agent payload can shrink the result but never corrupt the parse' is false
summary: Pipe and newline injection through a process name. Harness-verified: a name `x|winword.exe|SYSTEM|5|5` parses as name x, parent winword.exe, user SYSTEM; a newline in a name forges a whole row (name=sshd parent=systemd user=root parsed). Windows image names cannot contain '|'; Linux/macOS comm can. A local unprivileged user can disguise a process (benign name, parent and user) in the operator's tree and defeat the anomaly view. EXPOSURE is unresolved (a local actor on an endpoint influencing server-trusted agent output: E2 or none) so the finding gates pending adjudication. Fix now (server half): require cells.size() == schema width, count and show 'N rows unreadable', bound split_pipe at width+1 (also removes the 30-75x allocation amplification, 312 MB peak for a 4 MiB pipe line). The newline half needs agent-side escaping (file a W1 follow-up).

summary: A command whose terminal row has status >= 2 after at least one output frame is returned ready=true failed=false. poll_command only sets failed when there are NO output frames, so the partial head of a multi-frame answer (the agent flushes each 64 KB as its own frame, agents/core/src/agent.cpp:286) parses cleanly and is shown as the whole answer for the process tree, connections, hour list, DNS and ARP. The cut note fires only at 10,000 rows and the `__total__|N` trailer is skipped, never checked, so nothing flags the tear. The pre-fix code ignored status in the same way (d394d35ba echo_tree_routes.cpp:285-291), but this fix round rewrote this function to close exactly this class (r1 B1/B4). Fix shape: when terminal->status >= 2 set failed and error even if frames exist (and/or require a `__total__|N` trailer equal to the parsed row count); add a test with a failure terminal beside output frames (none exists). Raised independently by three Gate 8 reviewers in one wave; trigger unresolved (do_sql itself returns non-zero only before writing any frame, so a producer is a mid-flush cancel, kill or timeout), kept `likely` and derived from I3 per the absences rule; needs non-author adjudication only if it is to be released without a fix.

trigger: compromised agent stores many large frames for a command id, then an operator opens the tree for that device
classification_rationale: poll_command concatenates every frame into pr
summary: poll_command concatenates every frame into pr.output before any byte cap is checked. A compromised agent can store up to ResponseQuery.limit (100) frames of up to kMaxIngestBytes (2 MiB) for one command id, so one poll builds about 200 MiB, and /result holds proc, tcp and hour-list merges at once; the hour list has no byte cap at all. Old code kept one frame. Fix shape: sum frame sizes first, refuse over the caller's cap before concatenating, cap the hour list.
